    lpl = batch['log_prob_l']

    advantage_w = batch['advantage_w']
    advantage_l = batch['advantage_l']

    return ops.mean(loss)

    adv_w = batch['advantage_w']
    adv_l = batch['advantage_l']

    advantage_gap = ops.sub(adv_w, adv_l)
    advantage_norm = ops.normalize(advantage_gap)
    diff = ops.sub(lpw, lpl)
    exp_diff = ops.exp(diff)

    weighted_exp = ops.mul(exp_diff, advantage_norm)
    if weight is not None:
        weighted_exp = ops.mul(weighted_exp, weight)

    # Calculate loss = mean of -log( weighted_exp / (weighted_exp + 1) )
    # equivalent to -logsigmoid(log(weighted_exp)) but weighted_exp may be very small,
    # so we do explicit stable calculation:
    # loss_i = -log( weighted_exp / (weighted_exp + 1) ) = - (log(weighted_exp) - log(weighted_exp + 1))

    log_w_exp = ops.log(weighted_exp)
    log_denom = ops.log(ops.add(weighted_exp, ops.ones_like(weighted_exp)))
    loss = ops.neg(ops.sub(log_w_exp, log_denom))

    return ops.mean(loss)

ir.intuition: This loss models preference by the ratio of exponentiated log-prob differences relativized by advantage gaps, turning the pairwise difference into a probabilistic ratio modulated by advantage signals. Instead of additive difference or margin, it uses a relativistic multiplicative signal with logarithmic stabilization, promoting proportional preference scoring weighted by advantage ratios.

    adv_l = batch['advantage_l']

    adv_l_safe = ops.add(adv_l, eps)
    log_ratio = ops.sub(lpw, lpl)
    adv_ratio = ops.div(adv_w_safe, adv_l_safe)
    scaled_ratio = ops.div(ops.exp(log_ratio), adv_ratio)

    sigmoid_val = ops.sigmoid(scaled_ratio)
    loss_elements = ops.neg(ops.log(sigmoid_val))
    weighted_loss = ops.mul(weight, loss_elements)
    loss = ops.mean(weighted_loss)
    return loss

    adv_l = batch['advantage_l']
    alpha = float(extra.get('alpha', extra.get('hyperparams', {}).get('alpha', 1.0)))

    adv_norm = ops.clamp(ops.normalize(adv_gap), 0.0, 1.0)
    diff = ops.sub(lpw, lpl)
    score = ops.sigmoid(ops.mul(alpha, diff))

    return ops.mean(loss_terms)
